title: Prompt Caching
description: Understand Anthropic's prompt caching feature, how it reduces API costs and latency, and when to use it.

data.text: Prompt caching is an Anthropic feature that stores parts of your API request so they do not need to be reprocessed on subsequent calls. If you send the same system prompt, context documents, or instructions repeatedly, Claude can reference the cached version instead of re-reading the entire input. This significantly reduces both cost and response time.

Without caching, every API request processes the entire prompt from scratch. If you send a 50-page document with every request, you are paying to process those 50 pages every time. With caching, the document is processed once, stored, and reused — reducing the input token cost by up to 90% and cutting latency dramatically.

data.caption: How prompt caching works — cache vs. no cache
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Without Cache
    A1[Send Full Prompt] --> B1[Process All Tokens]
    B1 --> C1[Generate Response]
    end

    subgraph With Cache
    A2[Send Prompt + Cache Check] --> B2{Cache Hit?}
    B2 -->|Yes| C2[Reuse Cached Prefix]
    B2 -->|No| D2[Process & Cache]
    D2 --> C2
    C2 --> E2[Generate Response]
    end

    style B2 fill:#fff3cd
    style C2 fill:#d1f3d8

data.text: Prompt caching works at the prefix level — it caches the beginning of your prompt, which typically includes the system prompt and any static context. When you make subsequent requests with the same prefix, Claude checks the cache. If found, it skips reprocessing and goes straight to generating the response for the new content.

data.title: Prompt caching is most effective when:
items: You send the same system prompt or instructions repeatedly
You include the same reference documents or context in multiple requests
You are building a chatbot with a consistent knowledge base
You process similar requests in batch (e.g., analyzing many documents with the same rubric)

data.title: Prompt caching cost comparison
data.content:
Scenario: You run a customer support bot with a 3,000-token system prompt and receive 10,000 queries per month.

Without caching:
- Input: 3,000 tokens x 10,000 = 30M tokens
- Cost (Sonnet): 30M x $3.00/MTok = $90.00

With caching (90% discount on cached tokens):
- Cached: 3,000 tokens x 10,000 = 30M tokens (but at 10% price)
- Cached cost: 30M x $0.30/MTok = $9.00
- Savings: $81.00 (90% reduction)

data.text: To use prompt caching, you add a cache_control parameter to your API request. This tells Claude which parts of your prompt should be cached and for how long. The cache has a TTL (time-to-live) — typically 5 minutes for active use, after which the cached data expires and must be reprocessed.

data.title: Get the most from prompt caching:
items: Keep your system prompt and static context consistent across requests
Put the longest, most stable content at the beginning of the prompt
Use the same cache_control settings for similar requests
Monitor cache hit rates in your API dashboard
Batch similar requests together to maximize cache reuse

data.title: Cache hit rate is key
data.text: Prompt caching only saves money when you have a high cache hit rate. If you are sending completely different prompts every time, caching provides no benefit. The feature is designed for repetitive, structured use cases like chatbots, analysis pipelines, and content generation at scale.

items.question: Does caching work with the web interface?
items.answer: No. Prompt caching is an API-only feature. It is designed for developers building applications that make repeated API calls.

items.question: What is the minimum cacheable size?
items.answer: The cache has a minimum token threshold (currently 1,024 tokens). Prompts shorter than this cannot be cached.

items.question: Can I cache the entire conversation?
items.answer: You can cache the system prompt and static prefix, but the conversation history changes with each turn and cannot be cached in the same way.

data.title: Prompt caching recap
points: Prompt caching stores repeated prompt prefixes to reduce cost and latency
Cached tokens cost 90% less than uncached tokens
Most effective for chatbots, analysis pipelines, and batch processing
Keep system prompts and static context consistent across requests
Monitor cache hit rates to ensure the feature is working for your use case
